title: Alcohol industry involvement in the Moderate Alcohol and Cardiovascular Health Trial
authors: Mitchell G, Lesch M, McCambridge J
population: E-mail correspondence among NIH officials, researchers and alcohol companies on the MACH trial
funder: Wellcome Trust Investigator Award in Humanities and Social Science (grant 200321/Z/15/Z) to J. McCambridge.
authorConflicts: The authors have no conflicts of interests to declare.
result: The National Institutes of Health stopped the worldwide MACH trial in 2018, announcing its end in June 2018, after an NIH Advisory Committee to the Director working group review. Approximately two thirds of the funding for this $100 million trial was provided by five global alcohol producers (Anheuser-Busch InBev, Carlsberg, Diageo, Heineken and Pernod Ricard) through the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health. Participants were to be randomised to one drink per day or none. Soliciting the funding included convincing the companies that the study design supported their commercial interests, which the authors judge intrinsically biased.
